chapter_7_liquidation.description: Business ceases operations, trustee sells assets, pays creditors per priority
chapter_7_liquidation.accounting: Liquidation basis (report assets at net realizable value)

chapter_11_reorganization.description: Business continues operations under bankruptcy protection, restructures debt
chapter_11_reorganization.accounting: Going concern basis during reorganization. Fresh start accounting if criteria met upon emergence.

statement_of_affairs.purpose: Estimate recovery for creditors in Chapter 7 liquidation
statement_of_affairs.format: Show assets at NRV, liabilities by priority, estimated deficiency to unsecured creditors
statement_of_affairs.not_used_in_ongoing_gaap: Statement of affairs is supplementary liquidation analysis, not regular GAAP financial statement

creditor_priority: 1. Secured creditors (to extent of collateral value)
3. Unsecured priority claims (wages, employee benefits, taxes - subject to limits)

chapter_11_reorganization.debtor_in_possession: Company continues operations, management remains in control (debtor-in-possession)
chapter_11_reorganization.automatic_stay: Creditors cannot pursue collections during reorganization
chapter_11_reorganization.plan_of_reorganization: Company proposes plan to restructure debt, creditors vote, court confirms
chapter_11_reorganization.reorganization_items: Report separately on income statement: Professional fees, interest income (accumulated cash), gains/losses from restructuring

fresh_start_accounting.when_required: Both conditions met: (1) Reorganization value < postpetition liabilities + allowed claims, AND (2) Pre-bankruptcy shareholders receive <50% of new equity
fresh_start_accounting.effect: Company revalued as new entity. Assets/liabilities at FV. Retained earnings eliminated. New basis similar to purchase accounting.
fresh_start_accounting.reorganization_value: Fair value of entity (similar to enterprise value). Allocated to assets like purchase price allocation.
fresh_start_accounting.goodwill: If reorganization value > FV of net identifiable assets, recognize goodwill (or bargain purchase gain if opposite)

fresh_start_example.facts: Reorganization value $500K. FV of assets $600K, liabilities $200K. Old equity wiped out, new equity issued.
fresh_start_example.step_3: If reorganization value ≠ FV of net assets, adjust (recognize goodwill or gain)
fresh_start_example.in_this_case: FV of net assets = $600K - $200K = $400K. Reorganization value $500K. Recognize goodwill $100K.

content.troubled_debt_restructuring_in_bankruptc: Debt restructuring in bankruptcy context may use troubled debt restructuring rules or fresh start accounting depending on circumstances
cpa_exam_tips: Chapter 7 = Liquidation (assets at NRV). Chapter 11 = Reorganization (continue operations).
Statement of affairs: Liquidation analysis showing creditor priority and estimated recovery
Fresh start accounting: Required if (1) Reorganization value < liabilities, AND (2) Old shareholders get <50% new equity
Fresh start: Revalue to FV, eliminate old RE, recognize goodwill/gain based on reorganization value
Report reorganization items separately on income statement during Chapter 11

key_points: Chapter 7 = Liquidation, assets at NRV. Chapter 11 = Reorganization, going concern.
Statement of affairs: Shows creditor priority and estimated recovery in liquidation
Fresh start accounting: If (1) Reorganization value < liabilities AND (2) Old shareholders <50% new equity
Fresh start: Assets/liabilities to FV, eliminate old RE, recognize goodwill based on reorganization value
Creditor priority: Secured → Administrative → Priority unsecured → General unsecured → Equity
